items.title: Campus du Parc / IT'S Studio
items.summary: For twenty years, the former Nanterre School of Architecture was a ghost building, yet its spatial power never faded. Designed in 1971 by Jacques Kalisz and Roger Salem, it was the first public building of a vast social redevelopment project. It stands in the heart of the André-Malraux Park, conceived from the beginning as a true cultural city, surrounded by public buildings dedicated to culture such as the Théâtre Nanterre-Amandiers and the Paris Opera Ballet School. Abandoned since 2004, the site entered the Inventons la Métropole du Grand Paris 2 competition in 2018. The Campus du Parc project was born, curated by IT'S, in a shared path with Eiffage Immobilier, developer of the operation,

items.title: YUKI Office / UENOA
items.summary: YUKI office is the headquarters of a company in Kuki , Saitama, that sells organic vegetables under the philosophy of "thinking about food and health." The client asked for a building that would immediately convey the company's mission to anyone who visits: to deliver safe, trustworthy produce to consumers and to help preserve Japan's traditional food culture. After the Great East Japan Earthquake, the company used its own distribution network to support the affected areas, and it wanted a headquarters that could also support the local community in future disasters.

items.title: The XIV Ibero-American Biennial Comes to Brasília Under the Theme “Caring for Life”
items.summary: The Bienal Iberoamericana de Arquitectura y Urbanismo (Ibero-American Biennial of Architecture and Urbanism), known as BIAU for its Spanish name, is an international event promoted by the Government of Spain through its Ministry of Housing and Urban Agenda (MIVAU) since 1998. Held every two years in a different location across Latin America and the Iberian Peninsula, it recognizes, awards, and disseminates high-quality works that reflect the diversity of Ibero-American architecture and urbanism. Following its thirteenth edition, "CLIMAS: Acciones para el buen vivir" (CLIMATES: Actions for Good Living), held in Lima, Peru, in 2024, the XIV BIAU will take place in Brasília from November 3 to 6

items.title: Plaza Pochote Commercial Center / FAMM Arquitectura
items.summary: Plaza Pochote is a commercial development designed by FAMM Arquitectura in Santa Teresa , Costa Rica. Located along the town's main road, the project responds to a predominantly linear pattern of roadside development and the limited availability of public space within a rapidly growing coastal context. Rather than consolidating the program into a continuous commercial frontage, the architecture separates two built volumes to form an open plaza between them, making the space between buildings the primary organizing element of the project.

A movement that, within our discipline, is encouraged both through quality public spaces and through the powerful relationship between the public and private created through building facades. items.title: Promenade House / studio gm
items.summary: The Promenade House is a residence conceived from the experience of traversing and discovering the landscape. Situated on the shores of a lake and surrounded by an extensive garden, the house does not reveal itself immediately; access occurs along a winding path through the vegetation that gradually leads to the architecture. The path, therefore, is more than mere circulation; it structures the arrival experience, giving rise to the project's name: promenade, in reference to the act of walking and observing.

items.title: AA Apartments / Crearctive
items.summary: The project addresses the change of use of commercial premises to transform them into four independent apartments. Taking advantage of the open-plan layout of the original space and its generous clear height of thirteen feet (four meters), the proposal resolves the distribution by designing the void and working in section. The strategy relies on a central spine that groups the service spaces, which optimizes the layout of the building systems, frees up the perimeter of the home, and allows for the articulation of an intermediate level that makes the most of the height of the space.

items.title: Lion Green Road by Mary Duggan Architects and RUFFARCHITECTS Wins RIBA Stirling Prize 2026
items.summary: The RIBA Stirling Prize 2026 has been awarded to Lion Green Road , a housing development in Coulsdon, South London , designed by Mary Duggan Architects with RUFFARCHITECTS for Croydon Council. Comprising 157 homes across five residential blocks, the project combines privately owned and socially rented housing on a former car park. Presented annually by the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) , the Stirling Prize recognizes a building considered to make a significant contribution to the evolution of architecture and the built environment. The 2026 winner was announced at a ceremony at Old Billingsgate in London on October 15, marking the prize's 30th anniversary.

items.title: Making Room for Water: Floodable Parks in Latin America
items.summary: Walk along a river in almost any Latin American city and you will find stretches that have been straightened, lined with concrete, buried beneath roads, or pushed behind industrial areas and residential neighborhoods. Throughout the twentieth century, urban expansion gradually occupied riverbanks and former floodplains, while waterways were redirected or confined within infrastructure intended to control them. Yet the water continued to return. For decades, flooding has been the most frequent natural disaster in Latin America and the Caribbean, according to the Inter-American Development Bank .

items.title: Learning Through Practice: Why Architecture Students Enter Competitions
items.summary: On paper, entering an architecture competition is one of the most challenging things an architecture student can do. What draws students to them is the chance to experiment, approaching a loosely defined program that leaves room to test unconventional ideas and unfamiliar tools outside the rhythm of the semester. That distance from assessment is a relatively recent development, as competitions were once central to architectural education.

items.title: On the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction: "Resilience Starts at Home"
items.summary: Every year on October 13, the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction (IDDRR) draws attention to the ways communities can reduce exposure and vulnerability to hazards. Established by the United Nation s in 1989, the day provides an opportunity to consider how governments, communities, and professionals can strengthen preparedness and resilience before disasters occur. For its 2026 edition, the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) has selected "Resilience Starts at Home" as its theme, placing housing at the center of this year's campaign.

items.summary: Port Melbourne Secondary College (PMSC) is the first vertical school as part of Australia's biggest urban rejuvenation project, Fishermans Bend. Designed by Billard Leece Partnership (BLP), the school is within a designated precinct for advanced technology, innovation and education where, over the next 30 years, 80,000 people will live, work and study. The development gives Port Melbourne a new, forward-thinking learning hub for students and the local community who have access to the library, gym, food technology and art spaces after hours.

items.title: Architecture of Care: 6 Unbuilt Spaces for Childhood from the ArchDaily Community
items.summary: As cities change, so do our expectations of them. People are asking for more caring spaces: public places open to all ages and genders, nature within reach of every social class, and settings that foster connection. Few design intentions hold these together as well as spaces for children. This selection of unbuilt projects submitted by ArchDaily readers showcases different approaches to care-based architecture. Schools , daycare centers , a library , a youth center, and a new model for orphanages take on the mission of providing a safe and stimulating environment for children at every stage of their development. Not yet built but carefully designed, these proposals offer a glimpse into space

items.title: UN-Habitat Recognizes Five Approaches to Adequate Housing With 2026 Scroll of Honour
items.summary: UN-Habitat has announced the five recipients of the 2026 Scroll of Honour Award, recognizing contributions to adequate housing and sustainable urban development in Brazil , Myanmar , Pakistan , Tunisia , and the United Kingdom . This year's winners include a housing organization working with communities affected by conflict and displacement, a researcher developing building materials from local and mining residues, an Indigenous village in Brazil, a public housing agency in Pakistan, and London Mayor Sadiq Khan . Selected from 101 nominations submitted across Africa , Asia , Europe , and the Americas , the recipients represent a range of approaches to addressing housing and urban development

items.title: From Desert Heat to Northern Winters: How Container Architecture Adapts Across the United States
items.summary: Far from simply transporting goods from A to B, shipping containers have become a go-to building material across the US, forming the basis of everything from tiny homes to container pools, site offices to workshops. But given the size of the country, and the range of climates found within its borders, the approach to container architecture can vary significantly from state to state, even county to county.

items.title: ZAYMA Residential Development / 0studio Arquitectura
items.summary: Initiated in 2022, Zayma is a residential development comprising eleven units organized into three volumes articulated around a central courtyard. Conceived as the project's primary spatial device, the courtyard is more than a void between buildings; it is the element that establishes the relationships among the complex's diverse components. It organizes circulation, access, views, and shared spaces, while introducing vegetation, natural light, and ventilation into the heart of the project.

items.summary: Photographer Marc Goodwin has extended his Atlas of Architectural Atmospheres to Belgium , capturing the workspaces of architecture studios in Antwerp , Brussels , and Ghent . The series includes large offices such as B-architecten , POLO , and Binst Architects , alongside smaller-scale practices like Studio Okami , Stand Van Zaken, and Bruno Spaas Architectuur. Many of them occupy buildings with layered pasts from former workshops , to cinemas , and from storage facilities, to waterfront structures.

items.title: HENN Launches CarbonBudget, a Free Tool for Calculating Project-Specific CO2 Emissions
items.summary: Architecture firm HENN has launched CarbonBudget , a digital tool that calculates project-specific CO2 budgets for buildings. The new platform, free of charge, is a contribution for designers to help reach the 1.5°C target , a global goal from the Paris Agreement to limit long-term global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. As the construction industry is responsible for around one-third of global CO2 emissions, architectural design decisions can effectively contribute to containing global warming. The tool is designed to calculate whether the emissions of a building project located in Europe are compatible with the Paris Agreement target, based on specific inputs such as location

items.title: Building and Unbuilding: An Approach to Circular Timber Construction Addressing Material Waste
items.summary: In the face of the climate crisis and within the framework of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, the reuse of materials has become prominent in the fields of construction and architecture in recent years. From "urban mining" to life cycle assessments (LCAs), professionals, organizations, and researchers are exploring different solutions and strategies to address the same overarching challenge. Project (Un)Build is a research initiative developing reversible timber construction methods that use straps and friction pads to facilitate material reuse . It contributes to the ongoing debate and reflection on the act of building itself.

items.title: Pupunha House / Laurent Troost Architectures + Hana Eto Gall Paisagismo
items.summary: With the premise of preserving the existing greenery and creating a compact and efficient residence, the office Laurent Troost Architectures designed the Casa Pupunha, located in a condominium in the western zone of Manaus , next to an area of permanent environmental protection. Its landscaping was crafted by Hana Eto Gall, conceived through a direct dialogue with the Amazonian landscape. The name refers to the pupunha palm that occupies the center of the lot, preserved throughout the construction, and to the other plants placed around the residence, which become an essential part of the landscaping and architectural concept.

items.title: House 258 / Cornetta Arquitetura
items.summary: Built on a steeply sloped lot, House 258 arises from the principle of designing appropriately for the place, occupying the land and landscape with subtlety and respect while preserving the existing grove on the property. The result is an architecture that, on one side, opens up to the sunset and the surrounding valley, with its facade marked by the golden tones of concrete under the evening light, and on the other, immerses itself in the shaded and silent forest, illuminated by the filtered light of the treetops.

items.title: Yaesu Daibiru Office Building / Nikken Sekkei
items.summary: Project Background and Inheritance of Design Thinking - This project is the redevelopment of a tenant office building facing Yaesu-dori Ave., a landmark street in front of Tokyo Station. The former building, designed by leading 20th-century Japanese architect Togo Murano (1891–1984), long defined the character of the streetscape through its distinctive facade combining stone and cast aluminum components. At a time when curtain walls with an aluminum glazing system were becoming widespread, its pursuit of material richness, precision in facade composition, and responsiveness to the street suggested an architectural approach not solely dependent on style.

items.title: Beyond the Bunker: Lessons from Survivalist Architecture on Resilience
items.summary: "Let us take a hard look at the facts." With this direct and hardly reassuring sentence, the director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization opened The Family Fallout Shelter , a 32-page manual published by the U.S. government in 1959 amid Cold War tensions. The document taught families how to build shelters capable of protecting them from radioactive fallout after a possible nuclear attack and, through technical drawings and sketches, outlined solutions using concrete blocks, walls filled with earth or sand, underground structures, and ventilation systems. It was a survival manual that, in many ways, also functioned as a construction manual.

items.title: Climate, Density, and Spatial Layers: 18 Houses Shaping Contemporary Vietnamese Architecture
items.summary: Contemporary Vietnamese residential architecture stands out for its deep sensitivity to local microclimates and context. Detailed studies of weather patterns consistently drive strategic design decisions, resulting in buildings that act as adaptive shelters. Facing conditions that range from scorching summers to dry, cold winters, along with frequent exposure to heavy rains, storms, and floods, architects adopt protective facade elements and multi-layered spatial configurations to shield interior spaces from harsh environmental factors.

items.title: Dutchmoor Valley Guesthouse / SEEK Design + Architecture
items.summary: On a 5-acre farmstead in rural Indiana lies an unassuming three-gable shed structure, nestled among the surrounding trees and a field of wildflowers. As a complement to the main complex, which consists of a main house, pool house, barn, and garden, this new 2,700-square-foot structure serves as a guest house, providing a private and serene experience for visiting family and friends. When unoccupied by guests, it is used as a wellness and entertainment retreat for the property owners. It features two guest bedrooms with a shared bath and soaking tub, a fitness room, a living room with a wood-burning stove, a coffee bar, an entertainment room with a pool table, and a multipurpose garage.

items.summary: Living Along the Tropical Edge - Set high on a hillside overlooking the tropical landscape of Nosara , Costa Rica, Casa Cinco 7 by QBO3 Arquitectos emerges from the encounter between a privileged site, a distant horizon, and a precise geometric operation. From its elevated position, the property opens toward expansive views across the landscape, making the horizon not simply a backdrop, but one of the main generators of the architecture.

items.title: How Buildner's Iceland Slow Sauna Competition Winners Respond to a Volcanic Landscape
items.summary: Buildner has announced the results of the Iceland Slow Sauna architecture competition, developed in partnership with Slow Travel Mývatn. Set beside Þúfa – Private Homestay in the volcanic landscape of Lake Mývatn in northern Iceland, the competition invited architects and designers to create a compact retreat combining a sauna and greenhouse within a single architectural experience. Rooted in the Icelandic tradition of bathing as a ritual of stillness and renewal, the brief asked participants to explore how heat, light, vegetation, and landscape could shape an intimate place of recovery and connection to nature.

items.title: The House of Continum / Squelette Design
items.summary: An Autopoietic Intervention in Minimal Brutalism – The House of Continuum reimagines the spatial syntax of co-living with nature, transcending the traditional paradigm of a residential retreat. Grounded in the principles of critical regionalism and biophilic design, the architecture refuses to impose itself upon the landscape. Instead, it operates as a permeable pavilion, seamlessly assimilating into the genius loci (spirit of the place). Designed originally as a sanctuary for wellness, the built environment establishes an empathetic dialogue with the surrounding ecology.

items.title: Brick on Sticks Retail Store / DOT BOT STUDIO
items.summary: Along the dense commercial fabric of Domlur-Indiranagar, a G+3 structure on a modest 40×60 plot announces itself quietly, almost evasively. In a landscape where dimensions are more often associated with compromise than ambition, the architecture resists the instinct to maximize presence through bulk or spectacle. Instead, it operates through a meticulous calibration of structure, material, and intent. Two existing street-edge trees on the footpath inadvertently frame the building from the pedestrian vantage, their canopies forming a natural urban proscenium that mediates how the architecture is first perceived.

items.title: Amman Architecture City Guide: 11 Projects in a Capital Shaped by Migration and Stone
items.summary: Built across several hills, Amman has grown at a pace few Middle Eastern capitals have matched. The city has received successive waves of migration — Circassians in the late 19th century, Palestinian refugees in 1948 and 1967, the Iraqi population after 1990, and Syrians since 2011 — each reshaping its density and social profile. Locally quarried limestone , extracted from quarries across Jordan and required by law for façades since the 1970s, has become the city's only common visual denominator. Behind this material uniformity, however, lies a continuous dialogue between vernacular tradition and international ambition.

items.summary: Set within a quiet residential context, Patina House is conceived as an exploration of time through material. Rather than foregrounding form, the design allows materials, craft, and use to shape the experience of the home. The architecture settles into a composed stone envelope that weathers with exposure to the elements, while a curtain of hanging plants forms a living patina, softening the volume over time.

items.title: casa POP / gon architects
items.summary: Casa POP is based on the premise that there is no such thing as a standard user, and therefore architecture must adapt to unique ways of living. The original home, a 78 m² apartment located in Vicálvaro, was built in the 2000s under the rigid standards of the traditional nuclear family, resulting in a highly compartmentalized layout full of hallways. This distribution was obsolete for its owners, Santiago and Ángel, a couple whose lives revolve around enjoyment, knowledge, and culture.

items.title: Light Through the Wall: Indian House Interiors Shaped by Brick Jali
items.summary: A brick façade does more than define the façade of a house. When designed as a porous screen, it becomes an intermediary between inside and outside, shaping the atmosphere and environmental conditions of the spaces behind it. Across contemporary Indian residential architecture, brick jali — a perforated or lattice brick screen — has been reinterpreted with a contemporary sensibility, drawing on vernacular architectural elements.

items.title: Office for Future Converts Former School Into Housing for Displaced Families in Ukraine
items.summary: Office for Future is converting a former school in Stavyshche, Ukraine , into housing for 42 families displaced by the war. Developed for the Charity Foundation Housing for IDP , the project, titled "Dvir – The Shared Courtyard," reuses the approximately 1,900-square-meter building to create 42 apartments and 200 square meters of shared indoor spaces. The intervention combines the existing structure with new timber elements, an energy retrofit, and the transformation of the former asphalt courtyard into a permeable green space.

Taking place in Porto, it is held in a city that characterizes the issues at play: a coastal city, a historic maritime centre and Europe’s first protected wine region. items.title: Résidence Lourmel / MARS Architectes
items.summary: Built on a former parking ramp, the Lourmel student housing is conceived as an intermediate figure between the existing buildings and the central garden. Rather than creating a continuous volume, it is divided into four slightly offset blocks. Their shifts and rotations respond to constraints of distance, views and privacy, while opening diagonal perspectives, improving daylight and strengthening connections to the landscape. The volumes gradually recede towards the center of the block, creating a more porous relationship with the street. The existing courtyard is also fully re-landscaped.

items.title: Fire Severely Damages Jean Nouvel’s La Querola in Andorra
items.summary: A fire has severely damaged La Querola d'Ordino , a residential development in Ordino, Andorra , designed by Jean Nouvel in collaboration with Ribas & Ribas Arquitectes and Jordi Sala. The fire began during the early hours of September 22 and spread across the seven-building complex before being brought under control on September 23. Firefighters from Andorra and neighboring France were involved in the response, with authorities reporting no injuries. The cause of the fire has not yet been established.

items.title: Designing Domes in the Digital Age: From Concept to Preliminary Estimate
items.summary: Despite being among architecture's oldest structural forms, domes continue to offer possibilities for creating large, column-free spaces and working with circular or free-form geometries beyond conventional rectangular building types. Their evolution has been closely tied to changes in materials, construction methods, and design tools. Today, digital platforms are adding another layer to this process, allowing some of the decisions traditionally developed later in a project to be explored much earlier.

items.title: Ellen Browning Building / Hacker Architects
items.summary: The genesis for the mixed-use residential Ellen Browning Building arose when a group of close friends considered how they could preserve their relationships during their last years. Co-housing, with its spirit of community and shared living spaces, provided the answer. By developing their own residential building, the friends would be able to balance togetherness with the independence of urban living. The site they selected is set within a vibrant retail and commercial district along Division Street in Southeast Portland . Like many seniors, choosing to live in a walkable, amenity-supported and health-care rich city is an aging-in-place strategy.

items.title: On the International Day of Peace: Architecture Between Conflict and Coexistence
items.summary: Every year on September 21, the United Nations marks the International Day of Peace, an observance that invites global reflection on the conditions necessary to cultivate non-violence, social stability, and human dignity. Under the 2026 theme, "Invest in Peace – For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day," the international body emphasizes that peace is neither static nor self-sustaining. Rather than an abstract condition defined solely by diplomatic agreements, peace operates as an ongoing social process, shaped by economic equity, institutional integrity, and the quality of civic life across communities.

items.title: Bothaus Coffee - Sudo Developer Center / HCCH Studio
items.summary: Located on the lower floor of Sudo Technology's office and robotics laboratory in a tower along Shanghai's Yangpu waterfront, Bothaus is a small reception and exhibition space designed for the embodied intelligence company and its invited users. At the outset of the project, the client introduced an unusual brief: the space should have a "low-tech feel". We found the phrase intriguing. Rather than simply describing an aesthetic preference, it seemed to suggest a broader idea of the future — one in which technology becomes increasingly embedded in everyday life, and increasingly less conspicuous.

Spanning 28 countries, from Japan and Southeast Asia through South and Central Asia to the Middle East , Iran, and Lebanon , the book brings together 140 buildings and more than 150 photographs, placing internationally recognized works by architects including Kenzo Tange, Paul Rudolph, Balkrishna V. items.title: What Are Architects Escaping From? Ambition and Avoidance in Designing for Remote Sites
items.summary: Ask an architect what the hardest problem in the discipline is right now. The block of unmaintained postwar housing two streets from their office rarely comes up. What comes to their mind is the pressure differentials on Mars , or the tensile loads on a floating platform; because unclaimed ground has no one to negotiate with, no history to answer to, no tenant to remember the last renovation, which makes it considerably easier to design for.

items.title: Beyond the Replica: Digital Heritage and the Limits of Preservation
items.summary: A cave in Maharashtra can now be entered without travelling to it. Through a virtual reality experience developed around Ajanta , visitors can move through a digitally reconstructed version of the caves from somewhere else entirely. The project raises an architectural question: if architecture is experienced through movement, scale, sequence and perception, what happens when those experiences can be recreated outside the physical site? IITM Pravartak's Digital Ajanta project uses 3D scanning , filming, modelling and virtual reality to document the caves and translate that record into an immersive experience.

items.title: MAR - Conversion of a single-family house into two residential units / bruna studio
items.summary: There are approximately 13.5 million single-family homes in Germany, occupied on average by fewer than two persons. At the same time, there is a shortage of around 1.4 million housing units in the country. Many people remain in their large homes despite changing life circumstances. Converting parts of these houses into two separate residential units would make a significant contribution to resolving the housing shortage — and would do so without the need for expensive, resource-intensive new construction.

items.title: SAGA Space Architects and 3DCP Group Complete 36-Unit 3D-Printed Student Village in Denmark
items.summary: 3DCP Group has completed Skovsporet, a 3D-printed student housing development in Holstebro , Denmark , designed by SAGA Space Architects in collaboration with MS+. Located near VIA University College , the project comprises 36 ground-level apartments distributed across six building clusters, covering a total area of 1,650 square meters. Constructed over 12 months, Skovsporet applies large-scale 3D concrete printing at the scale of a residential development, combining printed structural elements with conventional construction methods. The project was developed for NordVestBO and is scheduled to receive its first students this month.

items.title: Assemble to Transform Grade II*-Listed Bromley Hall into a New Creative and Light Industrial Workspace in London
items.summary: London-based art, architecture, and design collective Assemble has recently announced a new workspace project in the English capital. Since its founding in 2010, the studio has built a community around craft and making by providing creative and light industrial spaces resilient to market forces, working as a platform for ecologically and socially engaged work. It recently secured a 25-year lease, with the option to buy, on Bromley Hall, an early Tudor-period manor house considered one of the oldest houses in London . The plan is to transform the site's three buildings, Bromley Hall (c. 1485), the Old Poplar Library (c. 1904–5), and the RedBox container building, into Assemble's largest works

items.title: JH Gwangan Mixed-use building / U.GA Architects
items.summary: Situated in Mangmi-dong, Busan , the site occupies a sharp, acute-angled corner where a dynamic, high-traffic arterial road heading towards Haeundae collides with the quaint charm of an old residential alleyway and antique shops. While this prominent location offers ideal commercial visibility, it simultaneously imposes a defensive burden on the residential volumes above: shielding the inhabitants from relentless urban noise and intrusive gazes. In response, the architecture does not retreat into a closed, defensive fortress; rather, it manifests as a "permeable filter" that embraces the cityscape and its intense sunlight while safely cradling its residents.

In response, the architecture does not retreat into a closed, defensive fortress; rather, it manifests as a "permeable filter" that embraces the cityscape and its intense sunlight while safely cradling its residents.

items.title: MAD Reveals Design to Transform 1923 Warehouse Into Danshuis in Rotterdam
items.summary: MAD , the architecture studio founded by Ma Yansong , has revealed the designs for Danshuis, a new dance center planned for Rotterdam , the Netherlands . Located on a landmark site in the city's historic docklands, adjacent to the Fenix Museum of Migration , also designed by MAD , the project is expected to open in 2030. The 9,500-square-meter center will transform an Art Deco warehouse dating from 1923 on the south bank of the River Maas. Planned as a center for the production, development, and practice of dance across different styles, Danshuis aims to bring together professional and amateur programs for different ages and levels of experience.

items.title: Digital Worlds and the Limits of Frictionless Space: Rethinking Scale and Materiality
items.summary: Historically, the way we design has been closely linked to the way we build. Architecture moved through physical testing , trial and error, projection drawings, mock-ups, and physical models : each introducing a new layer of abstraction, but still remaining tied to material, scale, and construction . The introduction of CAD significantly changed this dynamic. At first, it was largely understood as the computerization of precise geometry for construction. Over time, however, digital tools moved earlier into the design process, replacing sketching, physical trial and error, model-making, and other forms of thinking that had once kept scale and material close at hand.

items.title_ru: Центр спорта и отдыха в парке Коронации / архитектура hcma + дизайн + Dub Architects + FaulknerBrowns Architects
items.summary_ru: Спортивно-развлекательный центр в парке Коронации в Эдмонтоне, спроектированный совместным предприятием hcma Architecture + Design и Dub Architects в сотрудничестве с экспертами по велодромам FaulknerBrowns, предлагает редкое сочетание общественного центра отдыха с высокопроизводительным спортивным тренировочным центром. Его приподнятая велосипедная дорожка, необычно расположенная на целый этаж над уровнем земли и окруженная беговой дорожкой, позволяет размещать различные общественные пространства под ней, внутри и вокруг нее. Отличительной особенностью этого проекта является беспрепятственный обзор между наземным городским двором и велосипедной дорожкой. Это не только делает высокоскоростную езду на велосипеде заметной для пользователя.

items.title: ArchDaily Next Practices Awards 2026: Meet the Jury
items.summary: Since its launch in 2020, the ArchDaily Next Practices Awards have spotlighted forward-thinking architecture practices that are redefining the boundaries of the discipline. Over five editions, the initiative has recognized 105 practices from 44 countries, amplifying voices from around the world and fostering a global conversation about architecture's evolving role in society. Across the winning practices, recurring values emerge: contextual sensitivity, sustainable material use, co-creation with communities, experimental and interdisciplinary approaches, memory and heritage, social responsibility, and human-scale interventions.

items.title_ru: AART выиграла конкурс на подземную королевскую сокровищницу в замке Русенборг в Копенгагене
items.summary_ru: Датская архитектурная компания AART выиграла международный конкурс на проект Rigets Skatkammer (Королевское сокровище), новое подземное расширение площадью 1300 квадратных метров к музею в замке Розенборг в Копенгагене. Проект, разработанный в сотрудничестве с VEGA Landskab, Fogh & Følner и Artelia, предусматривает размещение примерно 600 квадратных метров нового выставочного пространства под историческим рвом, при этом частично восстанавливая воду, окружающую ренессансный замок Кристиана IV. Проект призван предоставить новые возможности для посетителей и выставочные площади для Датской королевской коллекции, которая включает в себя драгоценности датской короны и коллекции исторических костюмов и в настоящее время привлекает более
